clue.text: Rhetorical device encountered once before in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the phrase is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: encountered means met, and once (formerly) before was said afore, an old word for the same thing

explanation.surface: A writer recalls a figure of speech they had come across before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks AFORE as an old-fashioned word for before; MET AFORE spoken aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech applying a word to something it does not literally describe is a classic rhetorical device.

clue.text: Religious leader as father figure, ultimately

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word figure

explanation.surface: A churchman is cast as a paternal figurehead for the faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Roman Catholic Church is the most prominent example of a religious leader.

clue.text: Lots of teachers in part of England cut

indicators.note: cut says the county name is shortened, here to its usual written abbreviation

parts.note: Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Schools in one English region are losing many of their teaching posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a story about job losses, but it trims Staffordshire, an English Midlands county, to its standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of teachers employed at a school is its staff; several schools have several such teams.

clue.text: Links good, when embraced by some forming unions

indicators.note: when embraced by says the letter for good sits inside the women marrying

parts.note: women getting married are forming marital unions

explanation.surface: Good relations are made when people join together in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Structures spanning a gap connect two sides, so they act as links between them.

clue.text: Strange rite in earlier time a number regarded as ominous

indicators.note: in places the rearranged rite inside the word for an earlier time

parts.note: then means at that earlier time

indicators.note: Strange tells us the letters of rite are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd ritual from the past centred on an unlucky number.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an eerie old ritual, but 'Strange' only shuffles RITE to IRTE; the earlier time wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstition holds this figure unlucky, so many buildings skip a floor with that number.

clue.text: Part of problem — ploy men typically use

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tactic men often fall back on is described as a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something to work, as in the employment of force, means making use of it.

clue.text: Parties regularly selected, happening in place with bars

indicators.note: regularly selected takes every other letter of Parties, starting with the first

parts.note: an event that is on is taking place or happening

explanation.surface: Parties are being picked at intervals for venues that have bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests pubs and nightclubs; the bars are those on cell windows.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail is a building with barred windows and doors to keep inmates in.

clue.text: Press employee to have a half of real ale

indicators.note: a half of takes the first two of the four letters of real

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, broadly a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A newspaper worker fancies a half-pint of real ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a half' looks like a half-pint order at the bar, but it takes half the word real. Porter is a dark British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who gathers news works for the press, the newspaper industry.

clue.text: Striking achievement of American flier returning to base

definitions.meaning: a home run, a hit in US baseball that lets the batter circle all the bases
a homing pigeon, trained to fly back to its loft

explanation.surface: A US airman's feat on getting back to base.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: American slang for a home run, and a short name for a pigeon bred to fly home.

clue.text: Gallery in New York, for example, unopened

indicators.note: unopened says the first letter is taken away

parts.note: New York is one of the US states

explanation.surface: An art gallery in New York has not yet opened its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallery in New York' suggests a Manhattan venue; New York is the state, minus its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is the famous group of British art museums in London, Liverpool and St Ives.

clue.text: Constitution's supporter supplied ruler with an agenda, for example

parts.note: to have fed people is to have supplied them with food
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an gives the single letter A
an agenda is one kind of list

explanation.surface: A backer of the constitution handed the ruler an agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: In US history, backers of the 1787 Constitution and strong central government were known by this name.

clue.text: Seeker of proof getting nothing in maths wrong

indicators.note: in puts the letter for nothing inside the shuffled maths
wrong says the letters of maths are put into a different order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A student demanding proof gets a zero for getting the maths wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle known as doubting Thomas refused to believe in the Resurrection until he had seen proof.

clue.text: Steep mountain presenting dire threat in early part of day

indicators.note: in places the shuffled threat inside the word for morning

parts.note: morn is the morning, the early part of the day

indicators.note: dire suggests the letters of threat in a bad way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climb is threatened at dawn by a grim danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dawn danger to climbers, but 'dire' only shuffles THREAT to ATTERH, and 'early part of day' is the poetic word for morning.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine peak on the Swiss-Italian border is famous for its steep pyramid shape.

clue.text: Part of chore very onerous for people, without exception

indicators.note: Part of says the answer lies within the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some household tasks are a heavy burden for all of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying all people without exception is the same as saying all persons.

clue.text: Wordsmiths assembled work, in theory, so oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Authors gather work which is, in theory, rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' is padding here, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: People who craft text for a living are skilled with words, which is what wordsmiths are.

clue.text: Lack of care skin problem on head required

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A skin condition on the scalp is treated carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests the top of the body; here it is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting hastily without thought for consequences shows a lack of care.

clue.text: One with shattered nerves? Just the opposite

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: shattered breaks the letters of nerves up and puts them back in a new order

explanation.surface: A person with shattered nerves? Rather, one in quite the reverse state.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of something, as in a mathematical sense, is its opposite.

clue.text: Hoaxed over name, given stuff to swallow uncritically

indicators.note: over says the word for hoaxed is laid over and around the letter for name

parts.note: to spoof someone is to hoax or trick them

explanation.surface: Someone tricked over a name was fed lies to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone handed opinions ready-made, never made to think, is said to be spoon-fed.

clue.text: False alarm — it is related to war

indicators.note: False says the letters given are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A false alarm turns out to be connected with war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlike or military matters, as in martial law or martial arts, relate to war.

clue.text: Endures being torpedoed by a submarine

indicators.note: being torpedoed breaks up the letters of endures

explanation.surface: A ship holds out while being torpedoed by a sub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' looks like the attacking vessel but is the adjective: below the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, submarine means existing or happening below the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Hearing organ bishop in US city installed in neighbourhood

indicators.note: installed says the organ and the bishop are set inside the city

parts.note: NY stands for New York
the ear is the organ of hearing
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop with an ear for things is installed in an American city near by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is within the neighbourhood, a short distance away.

clue.text: Proposal to bring it back in satellite

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round word inside the satellite

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite

indicators.note: back says the word it is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A suggestion to return something to an orbiting satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: In a debate or meeting, a formal proposal put to the vote is called a motion.

clue.text: Record time

definitions.meaning: the written record of a meeting; to record

explanation.surface: Note when something happened.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the official note of a meeting; the other is a short unit of time.

clue.text: State capital

definitions.meaning: a US state in the Pacific Northwest
the capital city of the United States, in the District of Columbia

explanation.surface: A seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves both a US state in the north-west and the federal capital on the Potomac.

clue.text: Quest, the conclusions of which you can reject

indicators.note: the conclusions of takes the final letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: A search whose results you are free to dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A search or pursuit for something sought is a quest.

clue.text: Outlaw or gangster? It depends on the initial case

definitions.meaning: Robin ..., the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest
American slang for a hoodlum or gangster

explanation.surface: Is he an outlaw or a gangster? The answer depends on a capital letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sentence is a hint: with a capital H it is Robin Hood; in lower case it is a hoodlum.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw, and hood is US slang for a criminal thug.

clue.text: British vessels in Scottish waters

parts.note: urns are vessels for holding liquid or ashes

explanation.surface: British ships are sailing in the seas around Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships, but they are containers. A burn is the Scottish word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland, small streams are called burns, so these are watercourses north of the border.

clue.text: Note added to novel Thoreau wrote

indicators.note: added to puts the note after the rearranged name
novel means new, so the letters of Thoreau are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Thoreau writes a novel and adds a footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book Thoreau wrote but is the anagram signal; Thoreau is the American writer of Walden.
explanation.definitionFit: To be the author of a book or paper is to have written it.
